At turn boundaries, status apply/stack/decay/expire changes are reflected in HUD/feedback within the same turn flow, so the current status state is fully readable from UI feedback without log inspection. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

If combat encounters an invalid or expired status reference, the invalid effect is rejected, visible failure feedback is emitted, and combat state remains non-corrupted and playable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
On M1 combat surfaces, status-related UI text renders correctly in en and zh-CN and never exposes raw localization keys. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Status rendering, damage/mitigation resolution, and turn-boundary decay all execute through the shared existing status contracts/services path, with no UI-local rule path used for those outcomes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

UI-only modules do not define parallel status semantics for stacking, decay, or modifier computation; presence of a parallel UI status-rule path fails this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Implementation evidence for T75 is valid only if workflow-selection evidence explicitly selecting T75 appears first; if selection evidence is missing or appears after implementation evidence, acceptance fails. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0075WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Extend Combat UI binding and feedback tests to cover status rendering, status-modified damage/block resolution, and turn-boundary decay.

title: Bind enemy intent generation and preview to data-driven AI on existing intent surfaces
description: Replace fixed enemy attack preview with data-driven intent generation and preview while deferring enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrails to a follow-up task.
acceptance: Before any player action, the existing intent surface renders enemy intent generated from enemy AI behavior definitions as the single source (no fixed/hardcoded fallback preview), and the rendered intent can express attack, block, buff, debuff, and mixed intent outputs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Enemy behavior selection for intent preview uses the named combat RNG stream, while UI-only interactions (hover, drag preview, localization refresh) leave that stream state unchanged; this task covers intent generation/preview only and does not execute enemy action resolution or no-repeat guardrail enforcement. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

With the same deterministic inputs, the upgraded intent path produces repeatable enemy intent output, and this determinism is verifiable without invoking enemy turn execution or action-resolution paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T76 scope is limited to enemy intent generation and preview binding; enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrail enforcement are explicitly out of scope for T76 acceptance paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The upgrade reuses the existing intent surface nodes and binding points; no parallel replacement intent surface is introduced in this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Under deterministic seed/inputs, enemy intent preview generated from AI behavior definitions remains repeatable and visible on existing intent surfaces, and UI-only operations do not advance the named combat RNG stream. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene tests to cover deterministic enemy intent generation, visible preview, and UI-only RNG non-advancement on the upgraded intent path.

title: Integrate trigger registration and combat-time hooks into the shared combat runtime
description: Integrate deterministic trigger registration and card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks into combat runtime while deferring powers/relics/potions presentation and effect integration to a follow-up task.
acceptance: On the shared combat runtime path, trigger registration and execution order is deterministic for card-play, turn-start, turn-end, damage, and death-check hooks; repeated identical runs produce identical hook order and outcomes, and no second trigger stack is used. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Card-play, turn-start, turn-end, damage, and death-check hooks are each invoked on the shared combat runtime path and produce deterministic end-to-end outputs for identical command sequences (feedback/history ordering and state deltas). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

The shared combat runtime exposes one auditable trigger-registration path, and trigger execution consumes registrations only from that shared path, not from side-channel or duplicate stacks. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After integrating these hooks, combat completion ownership remains in the route flow; trigger processing must not finalize or redirect route completion on its own, and death-check outcomes must be consumed through the existing route-owned completion chain. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

This task introduces no powers/relics/potions presentation wiring and no powers/relics/potions effect integration into runtime hook execution; related behavior remains absent/deferred in this phase. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

When damage is lethal, death-check hook executes exactly once after damage resolution and before route-owned completion consumption; trigger processing itself must not finalize or redirect route completion. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
On non-lethal damage resolution, death-check hook is not executed and route-owned completion flow remains unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
test_strategy: Add deterministic trigger-order assertions through existing Combat scene suites for card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks on the shared runtime path.

title: Layer combat presentation feedback on top of deterministic state without mutating runtime logic
description: Track the presentation-feedback layer as a UI-only overlay on existing deterministic combat runtime, without introducing a second logic path.
acceptance: For every successful card play and every resolved enemy action, the presentation layer must emit the transient visible feedback applicable to that resolved outcome (including damage numbers, block gain numbers, card-play motion cues, and hit/action feedback where relevant) in addition to HUD updates, and deterministic combat outcomes must remain identical to baseline runs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When card play, hit, block, invalid action, or enemy action runtime events occur, the corresponding combat SFX hook must be triggered; if an audio asset is missing, action resolution must still complete safely and required visible feedback must still be produced (audio playback may explicitly no-op) without runtime failure. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Hovering or focusing a card must display a readable preview containing cost, type, target rule, and localized effect text, and opening/closing this preview must not mutate deterministic combat state or advance/consume RNG. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Hovering or focusing enemy intent must display readable detail for incoming damage, block, or status effects, and showing/hiding this detail must not mutate deterministic turn state or RNG progression. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

In reduced-motion or headless-safe mode, card-play motion, damage numbers, block gain numbers, hit feedback, enemy action feedback, and preview open/close signals must remain test-observable via deterministic nodes/events/log outputs without depending on wall-clock animation timing, and combat state plus RNG outputs must match deterministic baselines. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Card-play motion cues and hit feedback must each be independently observable as presentation-layer outputs, not only inferred from static HUD value changes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
Presentation feedback emitted through scene-local helper paths must not mutate deterministic combat runtime state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

For feedback dispatch on card play, enemy action, hit, block, invalid action, card preview, and intent detail preview, presentation-layer handling must not mutate deterministic combat state or advance/rewind RNG beyond the underlying runtime event itself. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

For card play, enemy action, hit, block, invalid action, hover preview, and intent detail preview, presentation-layer handling must not re-resolve combat effects, must not duplicate action execution, and must not mutate deterministic combat state or advance/rewind RNG beyond the underlying runtime event itself. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Extend Combat UI tests with observable presentation-layer nodes/events and verify they do not mutate deterministic combat state or RNG.

title: Unify combat defeat trigger by HP change event and single-resolution guard
description: Track defeat routing unification across existing HP mutation paths so any HP<=0 transition resolves exactly once.
acceptance: All existing player-HP mutation entry points (including end-turn and non-end-turn paths) MUST call the same logic-state HP update entry (single-source state-update path); defeat routing MUST trigger only on HP transitions >0 -> <=0 from that unified path, and HP changes that do not cross this boundary (<=0 -> <=0 or >0 -> >0) MUST NOT trigger defeat resolve. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Within one combat resolution, defeat resolve is one-shot: after the first HP transition from >0 to <=0, the observable outcome MUST be Defeat summary + Main menu exactly once; no later HP updates (including recover-above-zero then drop-again, or staying <=0) may trigger another defeat resolve or replace Defeat with Victory. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

When HP<=0 triggers defeat, route ownership remains unchanged from current behavior, and the observable outcome is return to Main menu with a visible Defeat summary result. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Each existing player-HP mutation entry point (end-turn and non-end-turn) must be exercised and shown to produce identical HP-change-driven defeat behavior through the same state-update semantics; any entry point that can cause defeat without the unified HP-change flow fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

HP-change emission/callback MUST be produced by the unified logic-state update path for every HP mutation update (not defeat-only), with test-visible evidence on both end-turn and non-end-turn entry points; defeat routing MUST be causally bound to that emission when and only when HP transitions >0 -> <=0. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

No parallel defeat trigger is allowed outside the unified HP state-update flow: if a code path can resolve defeat without passing through the unified HP-change emission, acceptance fails even when observable routing appears correct. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Implementation evidence for T79 is valid only if workflow selection of T79 is recorded first; if implementation artifacts appear before workflow selection evidence, acceptance is not met. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0079WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add/extend Combat scene tests for HP-change-driven defeat trigger on end-turn and non-end-turn HP mutation paths, and verify one-shot defeat routing.

title: Wire CombatScene to existing DeckService runtime state instead of local pile counters
description: Track CombatScene migration from local pile arithmetic to the existing DeckService runtime state as the first concrete implementation slice under T71.
acceptance: In CombatScene, draw/discard/hand HUD counters and rendered hand-card list are derived from DeckService transition outputs for draw, play/discard, and end-turn. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

After a card-play action resolves through DeckService, the played card instance is absent from hand and present in discard (or exhaust when rules require), and HUD hand/draw/discard counters equal the DeckService post-play state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

At end turn, hand retention/discard resolution is performed via DeckService rules, and the post-resolution hand plus draw/discard counters displayed in CombatScene exactly match DeckService end-turn state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Given the same initial DeckState and identical action sequence, DeckService post-transition state and CombatScene HUD/hand presentation remain step-by-step identical across repeated runs (deterministic parity check). Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

CombatScene must not retain or mutate authoritative local draw/discard/hand counters, and must persist plus reuse the same DeckService-backed runtime state across sequential draw/play/end-turn actions (no per-action reinitialization, snapshot rebuild, or fallback local arithmetic). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

After a draw action resolves through DeckService, exactly the drawn card instance(s) are added to hand according to DeckService order/rules, removed from draw (or cycled per DeckService rules), and CombatScene hand UI plus draw/hand/discard counters exactly match the DeckService post-draw state. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

CombatScene action handlers for draw, play/discard, and end-turn must not perform direct scene-local pile arithmetic (increment/decrement or recompute authoritative draw/discard/hand counts); scene state is updated only by applying DeckService transition results. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After draw and end-turn transitions, CombatScene rendered hand-card order (by instance sequence) matches DeckService hand order rather than only membership/counter parity. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

When a request is rejected or yields no transition from DeckService, CombatScene produces no local side effects: hand membership, hand render order, and draw/hand/discard HUD counters remain unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Add/extend tests for deck-state-driven UI counters after play card/end turn and ensure deterministic transitions remain stable.

title: Expose draw-empty reshuffle cycle through existing DeckService-backed combat runtime
description: Track reshuffle exposure through the shared DeckService-backed combat runtime rather than a scene-local reshuffle implementation.
acceptance: When a draw is requested with draw pile = 0 and discard > 0, combat must execute the DeckService-backed runtime reshuffle path, transfer discard cards into draw, set discard to 0, and complete the originally pending draw request in that same flow. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

With the same initial runtime state and current shuffle policy, the draw-empty reshuffle flow must yield identical post-draw snapshot states across repeated runs, with no task-local shuffle-policy override. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

After reshuffle-then-continue-draw resolves, Combat HUD draw/discard counters and reshuffle-related deck-state presentation must be derived from shared combat runtime bindings (DeckService-backed transition/snapshot) rather than scene-local arithmetic/state, and must match runtime draw/discard values. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When a draw request crosses a reshuffle boundary but the total available cards still cannot satisfy the full requested count, the runtime must consume only available cards deterministically, leave draw/discard in a valid terminal state, and avoid duplicate or corrupted card movement. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

When draw cannot proceed because both draw and discard piles are empty, the draw request must preserve draw/discard/hand and related runtime deck state without partial mutation, and deterministic tests must assert this guard behavior before accepting T81 evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs

The draw-empty recovery must be observable only through DeckService-backed runtime snapshot/transition outputs consumed by combat UI bindings; scene-local reshuffle arithmetic/state mutation must not alter draw/discard results independently of runtime state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Add tests that exhaust draw pile, verify reshuffle from discard, discard reset, and continued draw behavior without state corruption.

title: Add combat deck total display on top of DeckService-backed pile state
description: Track total-deck HUD and pile invariant visibility on top of the shared DeckService-backed combat runtime, not as a second deck implementation.
acceptance: 战斗进行中，Combat HUD 必须显示 total deck 计数器（独立于 draw/hand/discard），其显示值必须等于共享 DeckService-backed 运行时总牌数，并在任一会影响牌堆计数的状态变更后立即刷新；若显示值与运行时总牌数不一致即判定失败。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs

在共享 DeckService-backed 的战斗转换路径（play-card、end-turn、reshuffle）中，每次转换完成后的结果状态必须满足 draw + hand + discard == total deck count；任一转换后不满足即判定失败。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs
当牌堆计数不变量被破坏时，场景必须给出明确且可见的诊断型安全回退反馈；若仍静默展示不一致计数则判定失败。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs

本任务实现必须限定为现有共享 DeckService-backed 运行时路径上的 HUD/不变量切片；若新增并行牌堆状态来源或第二套 deck-state 实现则判定失败。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs
若 workflow 未显式选择 T82，实现入口必须拒绝执行且保持实现/代码状态不变；评审证据必须先提供 workflow-selection 记录，再提供实现证据。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs

在共享 DeckService-backed 运行时路径下，play-card、end-turn、reshuffle 后必须同时满足：HUD total deck 显示值与运行时总牌数一致，且 draw + hand + discard == total deck count；任一不满足即判定失败。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs

T82 的实现证据仅在存在可审计的 T80 与 T81 完成证据后才有效；若缺少 T80/T81 前置证据，T82 实现入口必须拒绝执行并保持代码状态不变。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0082AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add UI/state tests ensuring draw+hand+discard equals total after play, end turn, and reshuffle transitions.

title: Hand off CombatScene card play to the existing CombatService runtime
description: Replace scene-local card resolution with the shared CombatService and PlayCard runtime while keeping current scene ownership and leaving Warrior seed and Rage runtime closure to follow-up tasks.
acceptance: When CombatScene executes a play-card action, visible combat state mutation and outcome resolution must be produced from the existing CombatService + PlayCard runtime result, not from scene-local sample resolution. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0011AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After each successful play-card or end-turn action, the current Combat scene feedback surfaces must update hand/discard or exhaust piles, energy, HP, and visible feedback text to match the shared runtime result exactly, with no stale or divergent display. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

This slice keeps CombatScene as the current combat route owner and current feedback surface owner; card-play and end-turn wiring must not introduce a second combat owner, alternate resolution scene, or owner reassignment path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Warrior starting-deck seeding is out of scope for this task: Task 83 neither requires nor claims closure for starting-deck seeding behavior, and acceptance for this task must not rely on new Warrior seeding wiring. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Live Rage runtime closure is out of scope for this task: Task 83 neither requires nor claims closure for Rage runtime behavior, and acceptance for this task must not rely on new Rage closure wiring. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

CombatScene must not fall back to scene-local sample resolution when shared runtime definitions/contracts or runtime snapshot inputs are missing/invalid; the request must be rejected and visible state must remain unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When CombatScene executes end-turn progression on a valid snapshot, enemy-turn resolution and next-turn state must be taken from the shared runtime progression path rather than from scene-local turn arithmetic. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend Combat scene and acceptance tests to verify CombatService-backed card resolution and removal of scene-local-only play behavior while preserving current surface ownership.

title: Generate Reward offers from existing card drop pools on first entry
description: Track first-entry Reward offer generation from the current act and encounter context so Reward stops relying on placeholder card content and uses the shared pool path.
acceptance: On first entry to Reward, the system generates exactly three offered cards through the existing shared card-pool path using the current act and encounter context; placeholder content or Reward-scene-local generation must not be used. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CardPoolSelectionTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

Given identical act and encounter context under first-entry conditions, the shared-pool Reward offer is deterministic before any re-entry or restore logic; any differing offer fails this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CardPoolSelectionTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

For T84 in Chapter 6, acceptance validates first-entry offer generation only; reward stability and failure-handling outcomes are out of scope and must not be used as pass criteria. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CardPoolSelectionTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

Invalid-pool fallback is deferred to a follow-up task; T84 must not require, implement, or claim acceptance based on invalid-pool fallback behavior. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

If workflow has not explicitly selected T84, implementation execution must be refused and implementation/code state must remain unchanged; review evidence must show workflow selection before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CardPoolSelectionTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

Reward scene tests and integration tests are added or extended to verify first-entry shared-pool offer generation on the existing reward path; missing either scene or integration coverage fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_first_entry_shared_pool_route.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs

Reward first-entry offer generation must use the shared reward pool owner as the only authoritative source, and RewardScene must not cache or synthesize an alternative authoritative offer set outside that path. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CardPoolSelectionTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0084AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend Reward scene and integration tests to cover pool-driven first-entry offer generation through the shared reward path.

title: Complete Reward three-choice selection and confirm gating on the existing Reward scene
description: Track the completion of the current Reward interaction so one offer can be selected and confirm is gated through the existing Reward scene.
acceptance: Changing selection from one offer to another transfers confirm eligibility to the newly selected offer and removes confirm eligibility from the previously selected offer without creating multiple valid selections. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

Within the existing Reward scene, confirm is unavailable when no offer is selected and becomes available only for the currently selected single offer; attempting confirm with no selection does not proceed and leaves selection and lock state unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

The existing standalone Reward scene presents exactly three offered card choices on the current surface, and the selection/confirm interaction is completed on that same Reward scene rather than via a second confirmation surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

Within this selection-phase task scope, once confirm is accepted for the selected offer on the existing Reward surface, that interaction state is locked and rejects further reselection or repeated confirm attempts from the same interaction state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

This task covers selection-state completion and confirm gating only: reward resolution in this phase does not mutate run HP or run Gold, while deck writeback, skip resolution, and broader persistent progression remain deferred to follow-up tasks. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend Reward scene tests to cover single selection state and confirm gating on the existing Reward surface.
Workflow selection evidence remains a governance gate and is validated by Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0085WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs.

title: Generate route graph from existing ActConfig for the live Map path
description: Replace the hard-coded M1 map node list with route graph generation from ActConfig while keeping current Map surface binding and visual closure in a follow-up task.
acceptance: For the live Map path, map services generate and expose playable route graph data from existing ActConfig for downstream consumption; route ownership semantics remain unchanged, no scene-embedded hard-coded M1 source or fallback is allowed, and full scene-level presentation closure remains out of scope for this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/MapActConfigurationTests.cs

When configured ActConfig content is insufficient for the requested route generation scope, execution must deterministically refuse and keep route progression state unchanged; the flow must not silently fall back to or reconstruct any hard-coded playable route graph. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/MapActConfigurationTests.cs

T86 must preserve route ownership guard semantics before and after ActConfig-driven generation: map-owned route entry behavior remains unchanged, and non-Map owners are deterministically refused with route-owner-mismatch without progress mutation. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/MapActConfigurationTests.cs

T86 map-surface scope remains minimal: scene interaction only needs to prove generated route data can be consumed for route-entry decisions; when selecting a locked or unreachable node, entry is deterministically refused with no route-progress mutation; full scene-level route presentation closure is explicitly deferred. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

When requested ActConfig count exceeds available configured acts, execution must refuse deterministically and avoid partial act execution so route progression state remains unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/MapActConfigurationTests.cs

Generated playable route graph topology (node identity/order and declared reachability seed markers) must be consumed from ActConfig map content through map services on the live Map path; passing only by configured act count is insufficient, and no hard-coded M1 topology source may be used. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/MapActConfigurationTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend map service tests to cover ActConfig-driven route generation and deterministic refusal for invalid or incomplete map content.

title: Resume Continue into real Map or combat entry boundaries from autosave metadata
description: Complete the successful Continue path for Map and combat entry boundaries while deferring locked surface restoration for Reward, Shop, and Event to a follow-up task.
acceptance: [ACC:T87.1] When autosave metadata passes integrity checks and current route-ownership checks for a Map or combat entry resume point, selecting Continue must restore into the corresponding real node-owned Map boundary or combat initial boundary in-session, rather than stopping at metadata validation only. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_headless_resume_repeatability.gd

[ACC:T87.2] When autosave metadata is invalid, or the resume target is a locked Reward/Shop/Event surface in this phase, selecting Continue must remain on the existing blocked-state UX with the existing visible refusal behavior and must not transition into any playable boundary. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_main_menu_continue_blocked_message.gd

[ACC:T87.3] Continue restore eligibility must require both autosave metadata integrity checks and current route ownership; metadata presence by itself must not allow restoration. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_headless_resume_repeatability.gd

[ACC:T87.4] T87 must not restore into locked Reward, Shop, or Event surfaces; this phase is limited to Map boundary and combat initial boundary restore, and locked-surface restore paths must stay blocked. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_main_menu_continue_blocked_message.gd

[ACC:T87.5] Resume integration tests must be added or updated to verify both successful Map/combat boundary restore and unchanged blocked-state behavior for invalid saves or locked-surface targets. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_headless_resume_repeatability.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_main_menu_continue_blocked_message.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend resume integration tests to cover valid restore into Map or combat boundaries and unchanged blocked-state behavior for invalid saves.

title: Integrate relic acquisition, equip state, and player-facing display on the shared run path
description: Promote relic definitions into acquired, equipped, and visible runtime state on the shared run path while deferring combat-time relic effect execution to a follow-up task.
acceptance: On the shared run path, granting a relic definition records acquired and equipped ownership in the existing run inventory; no scene-local or second relic ownership store is introduced, and duplicate or conflicting grants are rejected by existing uniqueness rules with run inventory and equipped state unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs

After a relic is equipped on the shared run path, the run-path visibility state exposes that equipped relic for decision-time inspection; when no relic is equipped, the same visibility state presents no stale equipped-relic data. This task validates run-path visibility state only and does not claim UI rendering-layer assertions. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs

T88 is limited to shared run-path acquisition, ownership, uniqueness enforcement, and equipped-state visibility; combat-time relic effect execution remains deferred to a follow-up task and relic-effect combat semantics stay unchanged in this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs

Run inventory ownership for both relic grant and equip closure remains on the existing shared runtime path; this task does not introduce a second persistence path, scene-local inventory authority, or an alternative equipped-state owner. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs

On the shared run path, run inventory behavior grants relic ownership only for defined relic ids, rejects duplicate/conflicting/undefined relic grants with acquired ownership and equipped state unchanged, and keeps equipped-state visibility consistent with ownership. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs

If workflow selection has not explicitly selected T88, implementation entry refuses execution and keeps implementation/code state unchanged; review evidence includes the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

On the shared run path, granting or equipping a relic id that is not present in existing relic definitions is refused, and acquired ownership, equipped state, and run-path visibility state remain unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0088AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend run inventory and UI tests to cover relic grant, uniqueness enforcement, and visible equipped state on the shared run path.

title: Instantiate combat enemy runtime from existing enemy data definitions
description: Track replacement of placeholder enemy construction with data-backed runtime enemy instantiation while keeping current combat ownership.

Data-backed enemy instantiation must keep the current targeting ownership path unchanged, and must not add a new targeting ownership model or alternate target-resolution owner. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd; Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0089AcceptanceTests.cs

Data-backed enemy instantiation must keep the current enemy-intent ownership path unchanged, and must not introduce a parallel enemy-intent ownership model. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd; Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0089AcceptanceTests.cs

T89 scope is limited to encounter-time enemy instantiation and authoritative runtime ownership; visible stat binding and invalid-definition surface fallback are deferred to a follow-up task and must remain unchanged here. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd; Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0089AcceptanceTests.cs

Enemy data tests and combat runtime tests must be added or extended to verify that live combat instantiates enemies from existing enemy data definitions and consumes those instances as authoritative runtime state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd; Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0089AcceptanceTests.cs

If T89 has not been explicitly selected by workflow, implementation entry must refuse execution and keep implementation/code state unchanged; review evidence must include the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0089WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend enemy data and combat runtime tests to cover data-backed enemy instantiation in the live combat path.

title: Promote status trigger ordering and fixed damage rules into the live combat runtime
description: Move the existing deterministic trigger ordering and fixed damage rules into the player-facing combat runtime while deferring AOE and feedback consistency closure to follow-up tasks.
acceptance: In the live player-facing combat path, combat resolution must run through the existing shared combat runtime entrypoint so deterministic status trigger ordering and fixed-damage outcomes no longer bypass shared semantics through a scene-local path. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090AcceptanceTests.cs

T90 must use the current combat runtime as the single owner of combat resolution and must not add a parallel resolver, separate trigger executor, or alternate fixed-damage resolution owner. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090AcceptanceTests.cs

Any player-visible combat feedback changed in T90 must be limited to what is required to validate ordered trigger results and fixed-damage outcomes coming from the shared runtime; broader scene feedback reconciliation remains out of scope. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090AcceptanceTests.cs
T90 must leave AOE ordering and broader full-surface feedback alignment to follow-up tasks rather than changing those behaviors in this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090AcceptanceTests.cs

Automated tests must execute the live combat runtime path and verify deterministic trigger ordering together with fixed-damage exemption behavior on that path. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090AcceptanceTests.cs

If T90 has not been explicitly selected by workflow, implementation entry must refuse to run and leave implementation/code state unchanged; review evidence must show the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0090WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend combat rule tests to cover trigger ordering and fixed damage exemptions inside the live combat runtime path.

title: Expand the run summary into a stored-data-backed settlement surface
description: Upgrade the current run summary into a stored-data-backed settlement surface for outcome and route progress while deferring reward, relic, and resume metadata completion to a follow-up task.
acceptance: On the existing run-summary owner surface introduced by T66, opening a stored settlement summary must show the recorded run outcome and route-progress values from stored run data, and those displayed values must not be recomputed from live run state at open time. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0066AcceptanceTests.cs

The settlement surface must open from both victory and defeat flows, must not mutate current run state when opened, and reopening the same stored summary data must produce the same settlement content each time. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd

T91 must only add stored-data-backed visibility for settlement outcome and route progress; reward metadata, relic metadata, and resume metadata completion must remain deferred to follow-up work and remain unchanged by this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd

When stored settlement summary data misses required outcome or route-progress fields, the settlement surface must not recompute from live run state, must keep deterministic placeholders (Outcome: Unknown, Node Progress: 0), and must not mutate the current run state while opened. If workflow selection has not explicitly selected T91, implementation entry must refuse execution, no implementation/code state may change, and review evidence must show the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0091WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

The existing settlement owner surface remains the sole settlement presentation authority; no alternate settlement panel, transient recompute model, or second read-model may act as the authoritative source for outcome or route-progress display. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0066AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend run summary tests to cover outcome and route-progress visibility from stored data and route-independent opening behavior.

title: Promote architecture boundary tests into the main task line for Core-versus-Godot protection
description: Add xUnit-based architecture tests to enforce the three-layer boundary: Game.Core must not reference Godot APIs, and adapters are the only layer allowed to touch Godot. Source: docs/migration/Phase-13-Quality-Gates-Backlog.md (B5).
acceptance: T92 is promoted from backlog documentation into the executable main task line as a runnable guardrail that the active repository workflow can execute. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

The repository exposes an executable architecture boundary check that deterministically fails when Game.Core introduces any dependency on Godot APIs or Godot assemblies. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092AcceptanceTests.cs

The guardrail enforces that Game.Core stays free of Godot dependencies while adapter-layer integration points remain the only allowed boundary for Godot interaction. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

A passing verification scenario runs the architecture boundary check together with the required xUnit coverage in one pass and records the passing result as deterministic evidence for this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

An isolated temp branch or fixture with an intentional Game.Core-to-Godot dependency causes the guardrail verification to fail deterministically, proving the violating case is blocked. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

If T92 has not been selected by the workflow, implementation entry refuses to run, leaves implementation and code state unchanged, and records workflow-selection evidence before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0092WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Introduce a small intentional violation in a temp branch to verify the test catches it.

title: Add deny-by-default external process execution guard and audit coverage
description: Provide a single adapter for external process execution and keep OS.execute disabled by default. Allow only explicit dev-mode allowlisted commands and write audit records on any deny/allow. Source: docs/migration/Phase-14-Godot-Security-Backlog.md (B3).
acceptance: T93 appears in the executable main task path instead of remaining backlog-only, and review evidence shows this OS.execute guard work was promoted into the mainline task set. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs

When external process execution is requested, it is denied by default unless the request goes through the single guarded adapter boundary; direct OS.execute-style execution outside that boundary remains unavailable. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs

For each denied request and each request allowed by the explicit Windows-friendly dev-mode allowlist, the guarded external-process path writes audit evidence that records the allow or deny decision rather than completing silently. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/ExternalProcessGuardTests.cs

T93 deterministic gates pass only if xUnit tests verify deny-by-default behavior, explicit allowlist behavior, and audit evidence for both Windows-friendly dev-mode allow cases and deny paths. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/ExternalProcessGuardTests.cs

T93 changes are confined to the external-process safety boundary and its audit behavior, with no gameplay feature change or gameplay-surface expansion introduced. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs

If workflow has not explicitly selected T93, the implementation entry refuses to run and leaves implementation/code state unchanged, and review evidence shows the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0093AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/ExternalProcessGuardTests.cs
test_strategy: xUnit tests cover deny-by-default and allowlist behavior with SECURITY_TEST_MODE=1.

title: Validate security-sensitive signal contracts before wider runtime expansion
description: Add contract validation for security-sensitive signals (naming/arguments) and integrate into CI checks. This should catch accidental drift between signal definitions and expected contracts. Source: docs/migration/Phase-14-Godot-Security-Backlog.md (B5).
acceptance: A deterministic validation step verifies every security-sensitive signal against the expected signal name and argument contract, and the run fails immediately with a CI-consumable deterministic failure result (stable error code/category) when any definition drifts, instead of deferring detection to runtime. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0094AcceptanceTests.cs

The security-sensitive signal-contract backlog item is surfaced in the executable main task line so repository guardrails and CI can run it directly rather than treating it as backlog-only tracking. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0094AcceptanceTests.cs

T94 includes at least one intentionally drifted security-sensitive signal contract, and deterministic validation reports that drift as a reproducible failure. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0094AcceptanceTests.cs

At least one integration-level security signal scenario must assert the emitted signal contract (canonical signal name plus expected argument shape/order) in the passing case, and a drifted contract in the same validation scope must produce an explicit deterministic failing result (not skip, not silent behavior change). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/Security/test_security_http_block_signal.gd

When workflow selection has not explicitly selected T94, implementation must refuse to start and leave implementation/code state unchanged, and the review evidence must show the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0094AcceptanceTests.cs

Deterministic contract-drift failures are surfaced in a machine-readable form suitable for CI gating (stable failure code/category and failing status), so pipeline decisions do not depend on log text matching. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0094AcceptanceTests.cs

Integration-level deterministic contract-drift validation keeps a dedicated anchor independent from the pass-case signal emission check, so acceptance-to-test mapping remains one obligation per anchor. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/Security/test_security_http_block_signal.gd
test_strategy: Run headless GdUnit4 suite and confirm contract checks report PASS/FAIL deterministically.

title: Seed CombatService runtime from the Warrior starting deck on combat entry
description: Extend the CombatService-backed entry path so combat starts from the Warrior starting deck and shared deck state instead of scene-local placeholder hands.
acceptance: Starting combat through the CombatService-backed flow seeds the shared CombatService runtime from the Warrior starting deck and shared deck state, and the initial combat piles are not created from scene-local placeholder hands. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0024AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Entering combat through the T83 CombatService-backed path starts from the Warrior starting deck through that existing path and does not bypass it or fall back to a different scene-local start flow. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0024AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After Warrior deck seeding on combat entry, runtime deck data remains owned by the existing shared deck state, and entry does not create a combat-local copy or alternate deck owner. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0024AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0011AcceptanceTests.cs

Combat start uses only the existing combat-start entry path for Warrior deck seeding, and no second seeding route can produce a different initial deck state. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0024AcceptanceTests.cs

After Warrior deck seeding and the initial draw, visible Combat draw, hand, and discard counts match the shared CombatService runtime counts and stay synchronized as those piles change. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0011AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Acceptance tests are added or updated to verify that combat entry through the shared CombatService-backed flow seeds from the Warrior starting deck and shared deck state. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0024AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0011AcceptanceTests.cs

Combat scene tests are added or updated to verify Warrior deck seeding on combat entry and draw, hand, and discard synchronization with CombatService state after seeding. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

If T95 has not been explicitly selected by workflow, the implementation entry aborts before making implementation changes, leaves implementation/code state unchanged, and review evidence shows the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0095WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend acceptance and Combat scene tests to verify Warrior deck seeding on combat entry and synchronization between CombatService state and visible piles.

title: Promote Rage into the live CombatService-backed player runtime
description: Finish the Warrior combat runtime by wiring Rage state creation, mutation, and player-visible effect through the shared combat path.
acceptance: When the Warrior combat loop runs through the live CombatService-backed runtime, it must create or consume the existing Rage model from the shared combat path and must not read from or maintain a separate dormant data-only Rage copy. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

Rage promotion in the live runtime must use the existing player-state and combat-state contracts, with no new parallel Rage contract and no combat-local Rage owner introduced for this flow. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

In the Combat scene, any player-visible Rage or related status shown while shared runtime state is available must come from that shared runtime; when a shared-runtime reset snapshot is applied after Rage was triggered, the scene must remain aligned with shared runtime state and must not branch into an independent parallel Rage/status owner. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_task0096_rage_runtime_bridge.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

Rage values created or changed through the shared runtime must persist across the Warrior combat flow segments covered by this task, rather than resetting or diverging between segments. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

Acceptance evidence for T96 must include both Warrior acceptance tests and Combat scene tests, and both test families must be present in the recorded evidence set. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_task0096_rage_runtime_bridge.gd

Automated tests must verify that the Warrior flow can apply Rage through the shared runtime itself, not merely that Rage remains persisted later or becomes visible in UI. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

Automated tests must verify that Rage applied through the shared runtime changes combat behavior or results in a player-visible way, not only that a Rage value is displayed. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_task0096_rage_runtime_bridge.gd

If T96 has not been selected by workflow, the implementation entry path must refuse to run, leave implementation/code state unchanged, and record workflow-selection evidence before any implementation evidence appears in review artifacts. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

When shared runtime Rage already exists for the Warrior player, applying Rage through the live CombatService-backed flow must mutate the same Rage state entry (stack increase on canonical status id) rather than creating or reading any parallel Rage copy. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs

Warrior Rage application and resulting combat effect must be verified through the CombatService entry path used by the live combat loop, not only through isolated status/pipeline helpers. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0096AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend Warrior acceptance and Combat scene tests to verify Rage state application, persistence, and visible combat impact through the shared runtime.

title: Bind generated ActConfig route data onto the live Map surface and route states
description: Project the generated ActConfig route graph into the current Map scene so reachable, locked, selected, and completed path states remain visible and actionable.
acceptance: When the live Map surface binds route data, it must read node, edge, and route-state projection from the T86-generated ActConfig route graph as the sole source of truth; changing the generated graph or its precomputed states must change the rendered Map output without requiring a scene-local route definition change. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Binding the T86-generated ActConfig route graph and all subsequent route-state interactions must update the existing route-owned Map surface in place, and that surface must remain the only map presentation owner with no second map presentation path introduced before or after interaction. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

After generated route binding is applied, the current route-owned Map surface must keep the same existing node/edge visual convention mapping for reachable, locked, selected-path, and completed states, so each state remains visually distinguishable on the same presentation surface after rebinding. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd
The live Map surface must visibly mark nodes or paths that are reachable according to the generated route data. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd
The live Map surface must visibly mark nodes or paths that are locked according to the generated route data. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd
The live Map surface must visibly mark the currently selected node or path according to the generated route data. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd
The live Map surface must visibly mark nodes or paths that are completed according to the generated route data. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

After route-state changes (selection, completion, unlock progression), the live Map surface must continue to display reachable, locked, selected, and completed markers consistent with the same generated route graph. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Interactions must be state-correct: selecting a reachable node/path is actionable and updates route state; attempting to select a locked or unreachable node/path is non-actionable and leaves route progression/selection state unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

On first bind, if the generated ActConfig route graph already marks any node or edge as selected-path or completed, the live Map surface must project those selected-path and completed states immediately without requiring a new local Map interaction first. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_map_scene_surface.gd

If T97 has not been selected by workflow, implementation entry must refuse execution, leave implementation/code state unchanged, and record workflow-selection evidence before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0097WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend Map scene tests to cover generated route binding, visible route states, and actionable node selection on the live Map surface.

title: Restore locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces after Continue
description: Extend Continue restoration so valid autosaves re-enter locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces without changing deterministic offers or route ownership.
acceptance: Continue restores a locked Reward, Shop, or Event surface only when the autosave metadata is valid and the restore ownership checks pass for that locked surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

For a valid autosave, Continue re-enters the locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces without changing the locked offers captured in the save. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

For a valid autosave, Continue re-enters the locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces without changing node ownership from the saved route state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

For a valid autosave, Continue re-enters the locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces with the deterministic route state preserved from the autosave. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

For an invalid autosave, Continue keeps the T87 blocked-state UX unchanged and does not enter the Reward, Shop, or Event restore flow. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

An invalid autosave does not reopen any Reward, Shop, or Event surface through Continue, even when locked-surface restoration is available for valid saves. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_main_menu_continue_blocked_message.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

Resume integration coverage includes valid-autosave re-entry into locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces and verifies that the resumed surface matches the saved surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

Resume integration coverage verifies that locked offers are unchanged after Continue restores a valid autosave into a locked Reward, Shop, or Event surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

Resume integration coverage verifies that route ownership is unchanged after Continue restores a valid autosave into a locked Reward, Shop, or Event surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

If T98 has not been selected by workflow, implementation entry refuses execution, leaves implementation/code state unchanged, and records the workflow-selection evidence before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0098WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Resume into locked Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces must reuse the existing node-owned restore path; introducing any separate surface-specific restore owner or bypass path fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_main_menu_continue_blocked_message.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend resume integration tests to cover deterministic re-entry into Reward, Shop, and Event surfaces with preserved locked offers and unchanged route ownership.

title: Drive relic runtime effects through the shared combat trigger path
description: Finish relic runtime combat closure by executing relic effects through the shared combat trigger path after acquisition and display are already live.
acceptance: When a relic is eligible to produce a combat-time effect, that effect is executed through the shared combat trigger path, and combat results do not depend on scene-local or one-off trigger shortcuts. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0099AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0031AcceptanceTests.cs

Routing combat-time relic effects through the shared combat trigger path preserves existing relic uniqueness rules, and the change does not introduce duplicate triggers, duplicate ownership, or non-unique runtime state. This task changes combat-time relic triggering only; post-combat relic closure and broader run trigger closure remain unchanged after the task work. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0099AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0031AcceptanceTests.cs

Combat integration coverage is added or updated to demonstrate that relic-triggered combat effects run through the shared combat trigger path and that uniqueness and ownership behavior remain correct. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0099AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0031AcceptanceTests.cs

If task 99 has not been selected by the workflow, implementation entry refuses execution, leaves implementation/code state unchanged, and review evidence shows the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0099AcceptanceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0098WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend combat integration tests to verify relic-triggered combat effects execute through shared trigger paths while preserving uniqueness and ownership rules.

title: Promote AOE and multi-hit ordering rules into the live combat runtime
description: Extend rule promotion so AOE and multi-hit effects resolve in the same deterministic target order as the shared damage rules during live combat.
acceptance: During live combat, AOE and multi-hit effects must resolve through the existing combat runtime entrypoint, and any separate runtime path fails acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0100AcceptanceTests.cs

During live combat, AOE and multi-hit effects must use the existing shared damage-calculation rules, and any separate damage-calculation branch fails acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0100AcceptanceTests.cs

During live combat, AOE and multi-hit resolution must follow the shared deterministic target-order rules owned by the combat runtime, and scene-local target-order logic must not alter the result order. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0100AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Combat rule tests must be added or extended to verify AOE and multi-hit ordering on the live combat runtime path and must fail when that ordering diverges from the shared damage-rule order. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0100AcceptanceTests.cs

If T100 has not been selected by workflow, implementation execution must be refused, implementation and code state must remain unchanged, and review evidence must show the workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0100AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend combat rule tests to cover AOE and multi-hit ordering inside the live combat runtime path.

title: Align player-visible combat feedback with the promoted runtime rule results
description: Finish combat rule promotion by ensuring combat feedback surfaces always reflect the shared runtime result after trigger, fixed damage, and AOE resolution.
acceptance: Changes under T101 are limited to player-visible feedback/log presentation mappings over existing shared runtime results, and with identical runtime inputs/seeds the combat runtime outcomes remain unchanged while only surfaced text/indicators may differ. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

For trigger, fixed-damage, and AOE command paths, the combat scene must surface outcomes aligned with the same shared runtime result ordering (including trigger order) without introducing new combat rules or reordering runtime-owned resolution. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Player-visible combat logs and HUD indicators must be asserted against the same shared runtime outcomes for trigger, fixed-damage, and AOE resolution, including refusal paths where runtime state remains unchanged and feedback explains refusal. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

If T101 is not selected by workflow, the implementation entry must refuse to run, leave code and implementation state unchanged, and record workflow-selection evidence before any implementation evidence in review output. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0101WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend Combat scene feedback tests to verify player-visible logs and indicators match shared runtime outcomes after trigger, fixed damage, and AOE resolution.

description: Add a lightweight governance pass to keep late M1 runtime tasks sized for one deterministic closure per Chapter 6 run before additional role, card, and monster expansion begins.

Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0102WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Validation evidence for this sizing pass includes a task graph review, dependency consistency checks, and matching audit updates recorded in docs/gdd/t1-t69-m1-wiring-audit.md. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0102WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Outputs from T102 are limited to governance audit findings and task-splitting updates for Chapter 6 sizing, and the task does not deliver gameplay feature implementation. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0102WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

If T102 has not been selected by the workflow, no implementation work advances under this task and the recorded state remains limited to sizing review evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0102WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Validate task sizing through task graph review, dependency consistency checks, explicit T70-T101 scope coverage, and updated audit evidence in docs/gdd/t1-t69-m1-wiring-audit.md.

title: Split Continue restore validation between primary boundaries and locked surfaces in the review pipeline
description: Keep Continue tasks narrow at execution time by teaching the review path to validate primary boundaries separately from locked surface restoration.
acceptance: Review pipeline evidence must show Continue restore validation as two distinct lanes, one for primary boundaries and one for locked surfaces, instead of a single combined closure. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0103WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Execution-plan and decision-log evidence must both show that T87 and T98 are handled through the separated Continue restore lanes so each task can be executed and re-reviewed independently. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0103WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
If any task-file dependency still forces the T87 and T98 closures back into one run, T103 does not pass. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0103WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

T103 must remain limited to governance and workflow planning or review evidence for the split Continue restore validation and must not add gameplay feature implementation. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0103WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
If workflow has not selected T103 for implementation, no implementation work may advance and the task must remain evidence-only. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0103WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Validate execution-plan and decision-log evidence for separated Continue restore lanes and verify no task file dependency collapses the two closures back into one run.

title: Split combat rule promotion review between core resolution and surface feedback closure
description: Keep combat rule promotion executable in narrower Chapter 6 loops by separating core rule integration from scene feedback reconciliation.
acceptance: Planning/review evidence must define lane boundaries for core rule integration, AOE ordering, and scene feedback reconciliation, including per-lane input/output and review owner, and must not collapse them into a single closure. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0104WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Evidence must map T90 to the core rule integration lane, T100 to the AOE ordering lane, and T101 to the feedback reconciliation lane as separate deterministic closures with independent re-review records. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0104WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Task graph/audit evidence must prove each lane can be re-run and re-reviewed without forcing re-open or merge of the other two lanes, and must record CH06 narrow-loop scope per lane. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0104WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

T104 is accepted only when its output is governance and workflow planning/review evidence, and gameplay feature implementation completion does not satisfy this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0104WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

If T104 is not workflow-selected, outputs remain evidence-only and must not transition T90, T100, or T101 into implementation execution through this task. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0104WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Validate task graph and audit evidence showing separated combat rule promotion lanes for core resolution, AOE ordering, and feedback alignment, with explicit T90/T100/T101 mapping and separate re-review closure evidence.

title: Resolve enemy turn actions and no-repeat guardrails from the displayed intent path
description: Build on intent preview so ending the player turn resolves the displayed enemy action exactly once and applies no-repeat guardrails through the shared runtime.
acceptance: When the player ends the turn, the enemy action shown by the current intent preview resolves exactly once through the shared runtime path, and the next-turn intent is generated deterministically afterward. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Enemy turn resolution is one-shot per accepted end_turn command: after one accepted end_turn, enemy intent effects do not replay unless a new end_turn command is explicitly issued. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Only the shared runtime enemy-turn path may mutate combat state; any scene-local enemy-turn path invocation must be a no-op for combat state mutation. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Displayed intent resolution uses the shared runtime path and preserves intent-to-resolution identity (no pre-resolution intent substitution). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

At end_turn acceptance time, the runtime executes the exact enemy intent instance currently displayed to the player (same intent payload), and does not re-roll or swap to a different intent before applying effects. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
If T105 has not been selected by workflow, no T105 implementation changes are applied and task-related state remains unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0105WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Status-aware choice semantics are observable: changing relevant status inputs changes enemy intent resolution outcome according to runtime rules, while identical inputs keep deterministic outcomes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene tests to cover one-shot enemy action resolution, status-aware intent execution, and deterministic no-repeat behavior on the shared runtime path.

T106 leaves potion runtime closure to a follow-up task, and the deterministic combat loop covered here runs and completes without any implemented potion runtime closure. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
Deterministic tests assert the observable trigger order for powers and relics on the shared trigger path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
Deterministic tests assert that the Combat scene exposes player-visible and inspectable UI state for powers and relics. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The Combat scene surfaces runtime outcomes from power and relic triggers as player-observable combat results rather than inspectable state only, and deterministic tests assert at least one such observable outcome. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

If T106 has not been selected by the workflow, implementation work for this task does not proceed and task-related state remains unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0106WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add deterministic trigger-order assertions, visible/inspectable Combat UI state assertions, and at least one player-observable runtime outcome assertion for powers and relics as effectful combat participants.

title: Complete settlement metadata for rewards and relics

title: Split enemy intent review between preview generation and enemy turn resolution
description: Keep enemy intent execution narrow in Chapter 6 by separating preview generation from enemy turn resolution and no-repeat verification.
acceptance: Task-graph evidence in docs/gdd/t1-t69-m1-wiring-audit.md and execution-plans/2026-05-06-task-108-enemy-intent-review-split-governance-evidence.md identifies enemy intent preview generation and enemy turn resolution as separate lanes that are tracked independently, and does not present them as a single combined review path. Audit evidence in docs/gdd/t1-t69-m1-wiring-audit.md and execution-plans/2026-05-06-task-108-enemy-intent-review-split-governance-evidence.md demonstrates T76 (preview-generation lane) and T105 (enemy-action-resolution lane) are independently reviewable, and each review path explicitly states the other lane is not a prerequisite. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0108WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

Planning and review evidence defines no-repeat verification semantics: after the split, re-review of T76 or T105 must not trigger or require a recombined enemy-intent review lane, and duplicate combined-lane verification is treated as invalid evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0108WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

test_strategy: Validate task graph, planning, review, and audit evidence showing separated enemy intent lanes for preview generation and enemy action resolution, with independent T76/T105 run and re-review closure evidence.

description: Keep settlement tasks narrow at execution time by teaching the review path to validate owner-surface closure, reward or relic metadata, and resume evidence as separate lanes.

T109 deliverables are limited to governance and workflow artifacts for planning, review, task-graph, and audit evidence, and do not include gameplay feature implementation. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0109SettlementReviewLaneSplitEvidenceTests.cs
