test_strategy: Validate planning, review, task-graph, and audit evidence showing separated settlement lanes for owner-surface closure, reward or relic metadata, and resume evidence.

title: Drive relic runtime effects through shared run trigger boundaries
description: Finish relic runtime closure outside direct combat resolution by executing relic effects through shared run trigger boundaries after combat-path effects are live.
acceptance: Before non-combat relic runtime routing for T110 is considered complete, the combat-path relic effect route established by T99 must already be live and reused as the same shared run trigger boundary path; introducing a parallel non-combat-only trigger route fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd

When a reward boundary triggers a relic runtime effect, the effect resolves through the shared run trigger path and not through a scene-local post-combat patch. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd

When a node-resolution boundary triggers a relic runtime effect, the effect resolves through the shared run trigger path and not through a scene-local post-combat patch. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd

When a post-combat ownership transition triggers a relic runtime effect, the effect resolves through the shared run trigger path and not through a scene-local patch path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Across shared run boundaries, relic-triggered results keep uniqueness rules and current ownership intact, and the resulting state changes remain observable in player-facing flow transitions. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

On non-combat surfaces, routing relic effects through shared run triggers does not create a scene-local relic effect stack, and those surfaces continue to resolve through the same shared run trigger path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Repeated triggering across reward/node-resolution/post-combat boundaries remains idempotent: duplicate relic runtime resolution attempts are rejected, while accepted transitions preserve uniqueness and current ownership without introducing a scene-local relic stack. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

If workflow has not selected T110 for implementation, this task does not execute implementation work or advance task execution state. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0110WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend run and integration tests to verify relic-triggered non-combat effects build on the T99 shared run trigger boundary path, execute at reward, node-resolution, and post-combat ownership-transition boundaries, and preserve uniqueness and ownership without scene-local runtime stacks.

title: Integrate potions as visible and effectful combat participants
description: Build on the shared trigger path so potions become visible, inspectable, and effectful participants on the combat surface.
acceptance: In the Combat scene, each active potion that can affect a player decision is surfaced on the combat surface; if a potion is not directly visible, it must be inspectable from the same surface through an explicit player-reachable inspect action, and inspected fields must match the shared combat-owned state at inspection time. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Combat reads potion participant state from the existing shared combat ownership path and does not create, maintain, or rely on a scene-local potion stack as the authoritative source. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When a potion resolves through the shared trigger path, the Combat scene applies the player-relevant result in trigger order and records feedback/history entries that explicitly identify potion source and resolved outcome in the same entry without substitution by non-potion participant messages. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

For identical combat inputs, potion execution order and potion-related feedback/history are identical across repeated runs, and active decision-relevant potion UI state remains visible or inspectable from the Combat surface. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Add deterministic trigger-order assertions and Combat UI state assertions for potions as visible, inspectable, and effectful combat participants on the shared combat ownership path.

title: Drive relic runtime review between combat and run trigger closures
description: Keep relic runtime tasks narrow at execution time by teaching the review path to validate combat trigger closure separately from broader run trigger closure.
acceptance: ACC:T112.1 Planning and review evidence explicitly permits T99 and T110 to execute and be re-reviewed independently, with relic combat trigger closure reviewed in a separate lane from run trigger closure rather than through a single combined path. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0112RelicRuntimeReviewEvidenceTests.cs

ACC:T112.2 The task graph and audit evidence define two independent relic runtime review lanes (combat trigger closure and run trigger closure), and approval or failure in one lane MUST NOT be used as approval or failure evidence for the other lane. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0112RelicRuntimeReviewEvidenceTests.cs

ACC:T112.3 T112 completion evidence is restricted to governance and workflow artifacts that prove lane split and independent re-review readiness for T99 and T110; gameplay implementation artifacts alone MUST NOT close T112. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0112RelicRuntimeReviewEvidenceTests.cs

ACC:T112.4 Until workflow explicitly selects T112, any implementation activity or code delta MUST NOT advance T112 state, and recorded progress remains planning and review evidence only. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0112RelicRuntimeReviewEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Validate planning, review, task-graph, and audit evidence showing separated relic runtime lanes for combat trigger closure and run trigger closure.

title: Surface settlement resume evidence from stored run data
description: Enrich the settlement surface so stored resume-related evidence is visible without mutating or recomputing run state at display time.
acceptance: When the settlement surface is opened for a stored run, it shows the existing T91 owner surface together with resume-related evidence sourced from stored run data, and viewing that surface does not change run state or recompute ownership. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd

The resume-related evidence shown on the settlement surface matches the stored player-visible flow history for that run and does not display resume evidence that is absent from the stored data. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd

Before workflow selection of T113, no implementation behavior for this task executes or progresses, and task-related state remains unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0113WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add or extend settlement and integration tests to cover resume-related evidence visibility from stored run data while preserving the T91 owner surface and display-time read-only behavior.

title: Stabilize Reward offer lock re-entry and invalid-pool fallback
description: Build on first-entry Reward generation so the offer stays locked across re-entry and fails safe when pool context cannot resolve a valid offer.
acceptance: When the player exits and re-enters the same Reward flow within the same runtime boundary, the Reward offer shown on first entry remains locked and the displayed offer set does not regenerate, change, or reorder. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd

When pool context is invalid or unavailable and no valid Reward offer can be resolved, the Reward flow presents visible player-facing fallback feedback and does not render invalid or placeholder reward cards as if resolution succeeded. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd

Reward lock persistence and invalid-pool handling remain on the existing shared offer-locking path under the current Reward scene ownership, with no separate Reward-specific lock persistence owner or parallel lock path introduced for this behavior. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd

Reward scene and integration coverage is added or updated so automated tests verify both same-boundary re-entry lock persistence and the visible fallback shown when pool resolution is invalid or unavailable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd

Workflow-scoped gating for T114 remains enforced through deterministic acceptance references and tests, so task implementation cannot pass unless the selected T114 acceptance set is executed and validated under the existing lane. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_three_cards_rendered.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend Reward scene and integration tests to cover shared offer-lock persistence across re-entry, current Reward scene ownership preservation, and visible invalid-pool fallback.

title: Resolve Reward confirm writeback and skip through the route-owned return path
description: Build on Reward selection state so confirm writes the chosen card into live run state and skip resolves once without mutating the deck.
acceptance: Using confirm with any valid selected Reward card appends exactly the final selected card_id into the current live run deck state exactly once, and that writeback is already visible before the current Reward flow returns through the existing route-owned return path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

Using skip leaves the live run deck state unchanged and resolves exactly once through the existing route-owned return path; any second skip attempt is rejected without route or deck mutation. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

Reward resolution reuses the existing Reward scene, and both confirm and skip return directly to the same existing route-owned owner target without any extra intermediate owner or alternate resolution scene being inserted for either action. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd

Using confirm with a selected Reward card resolves exactly once through the existing route-owned return path; any second confirm attempt after first resolution is rejected and does not mutate live run deck state or route history. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Reward/test_reward_scene_route_roundtrip.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend Reward scene tests to cover confirm writeback, skip-without-mutation, reuse of the existing Reward scene, and single-resolution route return.

title: Bind combat enemy surfaces and invalid-definition fallback to data-backed runtime enemies
description: Build on data-backed enemy runtime so visible enemy surfaces stay synchronized and invalid definitions fail safe with player-visible feedback.
acceptance: Combat scene binds enemy name, HP, block, and existing visible enemy combat surfaces to the same runtime enemy instance as a single source of truth, and each visible value updates from runtime state transitions without scene-local fallback values or stale divergence. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Given an invalid or incomplete enemy definition input, combat rejects preview generation, keeps selected target, intent rows, and enemy name/HP/block/status unchanged from pre-input state, and emits player-visible refused and invalid-action feedback through the existing presentation path; it must not render synthetic valid enemy stats. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Runtime-enemy targeting, intent rows, and enemy status panel values (name, HP, block, status) are derived from the same selected runtime enemy identity in the same frame; when selection changes, those surfaces switch together without cross-enemy mixed state or an alternate parallel presentation path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Coverage asserts at least one runtime transition and one invalid-definition rejection path with explicit pre/post visible values for enemy name, HP, block, and one additional enemy-facing surface (status or intent rows), and asserts unchanged-state semantics on rejection; node-existence checks alone are insufficient. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
If workflow has not selected T116, this task does not execute or produce implementation progress for T116. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0116WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs

After an invalid or incomplete enemy-definition input is rejected, a subsequent valid input updates target/intent/name/HP/block/status through the same runtime path without latched fallback state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Add or extend Combat scene tests and integration tests to cover visible enemy stat binding, reuse of existing targeting and intent surfaces, and invalid-definition fallback on top of the data-backed enemy runtime.

title: External URL allowlist + safe ShellOpen adapter
description: Provide a single safe entry point for opening external URLs and enforce HTTPS + allowlisted hosts. Support GD_OFFLINE_MODE=1 to deny all network-like actions and write audit records. Source: docs/migration/Phase-14-Godot-Security-Backlog.md (B1).
test_strategy: xUnit tests cover allow/deny/invalid URL cases and offline mode behavior.

title: Secure file access adapter (res:// read-only, user:// read-write)
description: Introduce a file access adapter that enforces the allowed roots (res://, user://), rejects absolute paths and path traversal, and emits audit records on violations.
test_strategy: xUnit tests cover user:// allow, res:// allow-read-only, absolute path deny, and traversal deny.

title: Performance budget gate integrated into quality gates
description: Ensure performance P95 budget checks are consistently executed in CI and surfaced in the unified quality gates summary. Source: docs/migration/Phase-15-Performance-Budgets-Backlog.md (B1) and ADR-0015.
test_strategy: Run perf suite locally with a low threshold to force a failure and verify gate behavior.

title: Baseline-based performance regression comparison (optional)
description: Add an optional baseline comparison workflow that compares current perf metrics against stored baseline JSON and fails if deviation exceeds tolerance. Source: docs/migration/Phase-15-Performance-Budgets-Backlog.md (B2).
test_strategy: Use a small fixture baseline/current JSON pair to validate compare logic.

title: Observability bootstrap (structured logs + optional Sentry init)
description: Implement an observability bootstrap in Godot (autoload) to provide structured logs and (optionally) initialize Sentry SDK when configured. Source: docs/migration/Phase-16-Observability-Backlog.md (B1).
test_strategy: Run headless selfcheck and verify structured log output is produced.

title: Release health gate script (Sentry Sessions) + CI integration
description: Provide a Windows-friendly release health gate script that queries Sentry Sessions/Users and enforces the Crash-Free threshold defined in ADR-0003. Source: docs/migration/Phase-16-Observability-Backlog.md (B3) and Phase-19 backlog (B1).
test_strategy: Run in dry-run mode with stub data (or missing env vars) and verify failure is explicit and logged.

title: Build/export pipeline hardening (Windows-only)
description: Harden the Windows build/export pipeline: environment checks, consistent artifacts, and log outputs under logs/ci/**. Source: docs/migration/Phase-17-Build-Backlog.md (B1/B2).
test_strategy: Run export in a local Windows environment and confirm build artifacts + logs are generated.

title: Release channel + release profile metadata (optional)
description: Introduce a release channel concept (qa/internal/beta/stable) and generate a release profile JSON capturing channel + enabled FeatureFlags + build metadata for traceability. Source: docs/migration/Phase-18-Staged-Release-Backlog.md (B1/B2).
test_strategy: Run build/export with RELEASE_CHANNEL set and verify release-profile.json contents.

title: Privacy & logging guidelines docs (project-facing)
description: Create project-facing privacy and logging guidelines documents to consolidate existing scattered rules and reduce future ambiguity. Source: docs/migration/Phase-16-Observability-Backlog.md (B4/B5).
test_strategy: Doc review: ensure ADR references are correct and no secrets/PII examples are included.

title: Duplication and cyclomatic complexity gate (lightweight)
description: Add lightweight duplication and cyclomatic complexity checks suitable for a Windows-only Godot+C# repo. Prefer Roslyn analyzers / dotnet tooling and small Python scanners over heavy external platforms. Source: docs/migration/Phase-13-Quality-Gates-Backlog.md (B3).
test_strategy: Run quality_gates.py locally on Windows and confirm reports are generated and parsed.

title: Performance reports and history artifacts (project-level)
description: Generate a human-readable performance report and keep a minimal history artifact (CSV/JSONL) for trend tracking. This is optional for T2 but should be ready before any wider distribution. Source: docs/migration/Phase-15-Performance-Budgets-Backlog.md (B3).
test_strategy: Run perf suite locally and inspect the generated report files for completeness.

title: Dedicated performance gate workflow (optional)
description: Add a dedicated CI workflow/job that runs only the performance gate (headless) and uploads perf artifacts. Source: docs/migration/Phase-15-Performance-Budgets-Backlog.md (B5).
test_strategy: Trigger the workflow manually and verify artifact upload and pass/fail behavior.

title: Game.Core observability client (structured logs + PII scrubbing)
description: Implement a pure C# observability client for Game.Core: structured logs, breadcrumbs, and optional sinks (e.g., Sentry via adapter). Include PII scrubbing rules aligned with ADR-0003/ADR-0019. Source: docs/migration/Phase-16-Observability-Backlog.md (B2).
test_strategy: Unit tests validate field scrubbing, tag propagation, and sink invocation ordering.

title: Dedicated Windows release workflow (tag/dispatch) + artifacts
description: Provide a dedicated GitHub Actions workflow for Windows releases (tag push or workflow_dispatch). It should export the game, run smoke, and upload artifacts with consistent naming. Source: docs/migration/Phase-17-Build-Backlog.md (B3).
test_strategy: Dry-run on a non-protected branch using workflow_dispatch and inspect uploaded artifacts.

title: Optional code signing step (SignTool) for release artifacts
description: Add an optional code signing step using Windows SignTool, controlled by environment variables and secrets. No signing material is stored in git. Source: docs/migration/Phase-17-Build-Backlog.md (B4).
test_strategy: Run in a local environment without secrets to confirm it safely skips.

title: Export presets for multiple configurations (debug/release/demo)
description: Define multiple export presets (Debug/Release/Demo) and update scripts to select presets via parameters. Source: docs/migration/Phase-17-Build-Backlog.md (B5).
test_strategy: Run export for each preset and verify artifacts are produced and runnable.

title: Extend enemy intent runtime to resolve structured multi-effect actions from displayed previews
description: Build on T76 and T105 so a displayed enemy intent can execute multiple structured effects across current-turn and next-turn timing without falling back to description-only parsing.
acceptance: On one accepted end_turn path, the displayed enemy intent resolves more than one structured effect for the same enemy, including at least attack+block and attack+status combinations, and runtime does not open or require a second enemy-turn execution lane. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs

When the displayed enemy intent includes a next-turn block effect, current-turn damage resolves on the accepted end_turn, and the scheduled block is applied at the next governed enemy-turn timing boundary instead of being applied immediately or skipped. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs

The displayed T76 intent instance is the execution source of truth: the runtime executes the same structured effect bundle shown in the current preview payload, with no re-roll, substitution, or description-only fallback before resolution. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs

Multi-effect enemy intent execution is deterministic and one-shot: identical inputs produce the same ordered effect outcomes, and one accepted end_turn command cannot cause the same displayed effect bundle to resolve twice. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs

In combat.tscn, enemy HP, block, status, intent rows, and combat feedback update in sync with the multi-effect runtime state so immediate effects appear on the accepted end_turn and delayed effects appear at the correct later timing boundary. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs

If a multi-effect enemy intent payload is invalid, incomplete, or cannot be scheduled deterministically, the shared runtime refuses execution or surfaces an explicit fallback, and combat state is left without partial mutation from that payload. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0131AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add xUnit and GdUnit coverage for structured enemy intent effects, delayed next-turn scheduling, preview-to-resolution identity, and invalid-payload refusal on the shared runtime path.

title: Promote live relic rewards from placeholder text to a config-driven effect catalog
description: Build on the closed relic wiring path so relics that can actually appear in M1 runs execute real configured gameplay effects instead of remaining placeholder-only identities.
acceptance: Each relic that can be obtained in a live M1 run from the starting relic set or reward pools resolves to a real configured gameplay effect with defined timing, parameters, and execution boundary; if any still-obtainable relic only exposes placeholder identity text and no executable effect, acceptance fails. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs

Combat-time relic effects that are implemented resolve only through the existing shared T99 combat trigger path, and implemented non-combat relic effects resolve only through the existing shared T110 run trigger boundaries; any scene-local trigger authority or duplicate trigger path fails acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Live M1 reward pools and starting relic sources do not silently expose partially implemented relics: every relic without a real governed effect is either removed from obtainable pools or surfaced through a deterministic unavailable-for-selection fallback. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

The live relic effect catalog is configuration-driven rather than scene-hardcoded: effect timing, target domain, and numeric parameters come from governed definitions that can be validated without relying on CombatScene or Main scene glue. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs

When a live relic effect resolves at a combat or run boundary, the player-visible text and outcome attribution match the configured effect that actually executed; stale placeholder text or mismatched effect messaging fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs

Promoting live relic rewards to real effects preserves the T88, T99, and T110 guarantees for uniqueness, ownership, and deterministic replay: duplicate ownership, duplicate trigger execution, or nondeterministic reward-path mutations fail acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs

Acceptance includes xUnit coverage for catalog-backed relic effect definitions, live reward-pool eligibility, shared combat and run boundary execution, and player-visible outcome evidence for implemented relics; if any listed xUnit coverage area is missing, acceptance fails. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0132AcceptanceTests.cs

Acceptance includes GdUnit coverage for live reward-pool eligibility, shared combat and run boundary execution, and player-visible outcome evidence for implemented relics; if any listed GdUnit coverage area is missing, acceptance fails. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd
test_strategy: Add xUnit and GdUnit coverage for catalog-backed relic effect definitions, live reward-pool eligibility, shared combat/run boundary execution, and player-visible outcome evidence for implemented relics.

title: Add a pre-snapshot runtime modifier pipeline for reward entries
description: Build a governed hook between reward-pool selection and reward-snapshot locking so relics, events, and other run-state systems can add, remove, or mutate reward entries for the next reward context without editing pool files.
acceptance: A shared runtime producer such as a relic or event can register deterministic add, remove, or mutate reward-entry modifications for the next reward context before snapshot generation, and when that next context is first materialized those registered modifications are applied without editing the underlying reward pool file. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs

After reward_pool_id resolution and before reward snapshot lock, the pipeline applies the registered add, remove, and mutate operations to the entry list that becomes the next context snapshot, and the first reward-scene entry shows that modified result. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

If a reward context is already locked in the shared reward owner path, later runtime modifiers leave that existing snapshot unchanged; a later still-unlocked context using the same reward pool id starts from the unmodified pool baseline and only applies modifiers newly registered for that later context when it is first materialized. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd

The runtime modifier pipeline preserves deterministic replay and reward lock semantics: identical shared run inputs produce the same modified reward snapshot, and re-entering the same reward context returns the unchanged locked modified snapshot. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd

Registered reward-entry modifiers are consumed only by the next reward context they target: once a context is first materialized or locked, those modifiers do not bleed into later contexts unless those later contexts register their own modifiers. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Runtime modifiers are limited to governed add, remove, and mutate changes within the existing reward entry schema, and attempts to submit unsupported reward types or partially invalid entry payloads fail explicitly or are surfaced explicitly without partially mutating the target reward snapshot. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add xUnit and GdUnit coverage for pre-snapshot modifier registration, deterministic next-context application, already-locked context immutability, and visible reward-scene results after modifier application.
